task: Draft a short text to my U10 team parents: Saturday's 9am game against Riverside is cancelled because of flooding on the field, and the makeup is Sunday 2pm at Hollis Park, field 3. Ask them to confirm by tonight whether their kid can make it.
rewrite:
ambition:     A veteran youth-league manager opens with the cancellation, puts the new day, time and field in one line a parent can screenshot, and makes the reply a single word (YES or NO) so the headcount can be tallied at a glance.
agency:       The raw material is the league's cancellation notice and the team's parent group thread. Neither is in reach, so this uses only the facts given (Saturday 9am vs Riverside cancelled for field flooding; makeup Sunday 2pm, Hollis Park, field 3) and invents no arrival time, address or other detail.
acceleration: Plain group SMS, the format parents already read on a phone. The reply-YES/NO convention replaces a back-and-forth about who can come.
accuracy:     Outside the model, the parents' replies by tonight are the real test. The closest proxy now is to check that the day, time, field and deadline match your message exactly and can all be found in one glance.

deeper task:
Write a short text message from me, the U10 coach, to the team parents. It should say that Saturday's 9am game against Riverside is cancelled because of flooding on the field, and that the makeup game is Sunday at 2pm at Hollis Park, field 3. Open with the cancellation, give the makeup day, time and field together on one easy-to-find line, and ask parents to reply YES or NO by tonight to say whether their kid can make it. Keep the tone friendly and brief, as one text, with no extra details beyond what I've given. Leave a blank for my name at the end.

answers.plain:
Here's a draft:

---

Hi U10 families! Saturday's 9am game vs. Riverside is cancelled because of flooding on the field. The makeup game is **Sunday at 2pm at Hollis Park, field 3**. Please reply by tonight to let me know whether your kid can make it. Thanks!

---

If you'd like, I can add a line about arrival time (for example, "arrive by 1:30 for warm-ups") or make it more casual.
answers.nudge:
Here's a draft that works as a group text. It's short, puts the change first, and makes replying easy.

**Main version**

> Hi U10 families, Saturday's 9am game vs. Riverside is **cancelled** because of flooding on the field.
>
> Makeup game: **Sunday, 2:00pm at Hollis Park, Field 3.**
>
> Please reply by **tonight** with YES or NO so we know if your player can make it. If we're short on numbers, I'll let everyone know tomorrow morning. Thanks for your flexibility!
>
> – [Your name]

**Why I wrote it this way**
- **The cancellation and the new time come first.** Parents skim, and the main thing is that Saturday is off and Sunday is on.
- **It asks for a one-word reply.** YES or NO is easier to answer and easier for you to count than a longer message.
- **It says what happens next.** Parents know when they'll hear back, so you won't get a string of follow-up texts.

**Optional tweaks**
- If you use a team app (TeamSnap, GameChanger, etc.), add "Please also update your RSVP in the app" so the roster stays accurate.
- If you want to know why a player can't come, change the ask to "Reply YES or NO (and let me know if you have a conflict)."
- If there's a minimum number of players you need, say so, for example "We need at least 7 to play." That way parents understand why the reply matters.
- Add a reminder for tonight, like a second text around 6pm to anyone who hasn't answered.

Before you send, check two things I couldn't confirm: that the field at Hollis Park is open at 2pm Sunday, and that Riverside has agreed to the new time. If either isn't settled yet, change "Makeup game" to "Proposed makeup game."
